name: Improper Privilege Management
title: CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
ai_text: In AI software, improper privilege management shows up in tools that hand out more access than a user's role should allow. The two CVEs here sit in an LLM chat interface and an MCP server. In Open WebUI, a non-admin account can delete a shared external connection, a change that should belong to administrators. In ArcadeDB's MCP server, a read-only user can change server settings. Both are reached through the normal interface a user already has, with no extra access needed. The result is that low-privilege users can alter shared resources or server configuration, which can disrupt other users and weaken the boundary between roles.
description: The product does not properly assign, modify, track, or check privileges for an actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

mitigations.description: Very carefully manage the setting, management, and handling of privileges. Explicitly manage trust zones in the software.
Follow the principle of least privilege when assigning access rights to entities in a software system.
Consider following the principle of separation of privilege. Require multiple conditions to be met before permitting access to a system resource.
